stem: Alanine, $\text{H}_2\text{NCH(CH}_3\text{)CO}_2\text{H}$, and glutamic acid, $\text{H}_2\text{NCH(CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H)CO}_2\text{H}$, are two naturally occurring amino acids.

(b)
(c)(i)
parts.stem: The mass spectrum of glutamic acid, $\text{H}_2\text{NCH(CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H)CO}_2\text{H}$, is obtained.
parts.text: State the $m/e$ value of the molecular ion peak in this spectrum.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
The spectrum has peaks with $m/e$ values of 88 and 131.

Draw the structures of the ions responsible for these peaks.

| :--- | :--- |
| 88 |  |
| 131 |  |

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem: At pH 11 alanine exists as $\text{H}_2\text{NCH(CH}_3\text{)CO}_2^-$ ions and glutamic acid exists as $\text{H}_2\text{NCH(CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2^-\text{)CO}_2^-$ ions. A mixture of alanine and glutamic acid at pH 11 is subjected to electrophoresis.
parts.text: State how the mixture can be maintained at pH 11 during electrophoresis.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Draw a fully labelled diagram for the apparatus that would be used to carry out this electrophoresis. Your diagram should include the position of the mixture of alanine and glutamic acid at the start of the electrophoresis experiment.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text: Identify the electrode that each amino acid travels towards during electrophoresis at pH 11.

parts.label: (d)(iv)
parts.text:
In a particular electrophoresis experiment at pH 11, the glutamic acid travels $3.4\text{ cm}$. Alanine travels a shorter distance.

Explain the factors that account for the difference in the distances travelled.
